newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia says no foreigners invited to poll.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia says no foreigners invited to poll.

text.p: Indonesian President Suharto has overturned a plan to invite foreign observers to the nation's May general elections, the official Antara news agency reported on Wednesday.

"I asked the president regarding the matter and he said that our government does not intend to invite them (foreigners)," Attorney-General Singgih told reporters after meeting with Suharto on Tuesday.
Interior Minister Yogie Memet, who heads the election implementation committee, said earlier this month that neighbouring and foreign countries would be invited to monitor the poll on May 29.

However, Singgih, also head of the official General Election Supervision Committee, said foreigners would be welcome to receive information on the election but if they wanted to observe polling places they would have ask permission of the poll organisers.
Singgih said those who do not have a letter from the authorities will be banned from polling places.
"Even a high-ranking officer could not enter the area if he does not have this letter," he said.

Indonesians will elect national, provincial and local legislators chosen from the three sanctioned parties -- the ruling Golkar, the Moslem-oriented United Development Party (PPP) and divided Christian-Nationalist Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI).
Golkar has set itself a target of around 70 percent of the vote. Campaigning is tightly restricted by government regulations and limited to mostly television debates.
